$comment: Lines a conforming client must refuse. Refusing means reporting a malformed frame, not crashing and not silently substituting a default: a shell that accepts these has invented a protocol of its own.

cases.name: truncated-json
cases.why: A frame cut off mid-object, which is what a half-written pipe looks like.

cases.name: missing-protocol-version
cases.why: The version is what makes the frame interpretable at all; there is no default for it.

cases.name: missing-command
cases.why: A request that names no command cannot be dispatched.

cases.name: unknown-owner
cases.why: Owner is a closed set. An unrecognised owner must not fall back to none, because none is claimable-by-nobody and would read as a release.

cases.name: generation-as-string
cases.why: Generations are compared numerically. A string that looks like a number is not one.

cases.name: payload-is-an-array
cases.why: The payload is an object. An array here means the sender is speaking a different protocol.

cases.name: response-missing-ok
cases.why: `ok` is how a client decides between payload and error. Guessing it is how a failure gets read as a success.

cases.name: empty-line
cases.why: A blank line is not a frame. It arrives when a process is closing.
